  CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  CITY COUNCIL

How to Submit Public Comment:

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
 ````
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, November 7, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Menchaca
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH
  B. LUNG CANCER AWARENESS MONTH
  C. UNITED AGAINST HATE WEEK
  D. ATHENS SERVICES UPDATE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 17, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are
  presented to the City Council for review and approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2023
  FOR THE GENERAL FUND AND MISSION PLAYHOUSE FUND

  The budget update incorporates the actual revenue received and
  expenditures that have occurred through September 30, 2023, and projects
  the financial results for the year ending on June 30, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  D. CITY CYBER SECURITY APPLICATION SUBSCRIPTION IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $40,513

  On September 2022, City Council approved DarkTrace Cyber Security
  application for the Police Departments IT network. Due to its success and
  effectiveness in detecting and preventing malicious traffic, City IT desires to
  extend the DarkTrace Cyber Security application to the remainder of the City’s
  IT network to bolster the City’s security posture. The subscription with
  DarkTrace is for a period of twenty-six and a half months. The total costs for
  the entire agreement period is $40,513, which is an annualized amount of
  about $18,345 per 12 month period. Funds have been appropriated in the
  fiscal year 2023-2024 Information Technology IS fund for this purchase (130-
  707-00-21-116).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a subscription agreement with DarkTrace Cyber Security application in
  the amount of $40,513 from July 17, 2023 to September 29, 2025.

  E. 2024 CITY COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE

  The City Council is scheduled to meet regularly on the first and third Tuesdays
  of each month. In the past, meeting cancellations have been decided on as
  the year progresses, due to holidays and/or lack of business items. There are
  nominal savings in staff time and utility costs for cancelled meetings.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the 2024 City Council
  meeting schedule as outlined in this report.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 23-70 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED SALARY
  SCHEDULE TO INCORPORATE THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA 2024
  MINIMUM WAGE RATE

  On January 1, 2024, the State minimum wage will increase to $16.00 per hour,
  which represents a 3.03% increase to the current minimum wage. Staff
  recommends increasing all part-time positions classifications by 3.03% to
  maintain minimum wage compliance and internal pay differentials among all
  part-time limited-service positions. The rate increase would be implemented
  with the pay period beginning on December 30, 2023. There are
  approximately 80 active part-time employees affected by the minimum wage
  increase. The minimum wage adjustment is expected to have an annualized
  cost impact of $28,674, which is spread over all departments. The cost impact
  for FY 2023-24 is $14,337, with the General Fund incurring $7,890 (55.0%) and
  special funds incurring $6,447 (45.0%) of the total increase. An additional
  appropriation of $7,890 in general funds and $6,447 in various other special
  funds is needed to cover the increase to part-time salaries in FY 2023-24.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  4
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-70, which
  amends the City’s authorized Salary Schedule by increasing the pay range of
  all part-time position classifications by the 2024 minimum wage requirement,
  effective December 30, 2023, and increases the General Fund appropriations
  $7,890 and various other special funds $6,447 to cover increases costs to part-
  time position salaries for FY 2023-24.

  G. AWARD  CONSTRUCTION  CONTRACT  NO.  23-06  TO  HHS
  CONSTRUCTION LLC FOR THE ADAPTIVE/TRAFFIC RESPONSIVE SIGNAL
  CONTROL PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF $4,584,108.50 PLUS A 10%
  CONTINGENCY

  HHS Construction LLC was the lowest responsive bidder for the
  Adaptive/Traffic Responsive Signal Control Project. The project aims to
  alleviate congestion, improve traffic safety, and reduce travel times, fuel
  consumption and pollution. The original project scope proposed to improve
  traffic progression along Valley Boulevard and San Gabriel Boulevard within
  the City by installing fiber-optic connectivity between the signals and a central
  traffic management system located in the Public Works Facility. The additional
  reallocation of funds allowed the following arterial sections to be included in
  the scope of work: Las Tunas Drive within the City; Del Mar Avenue from
  Valley Boulevard to Las Tunas Drive; and Mission Road from Del Mar Avenue
  to west of the City limit. Funds are available in the Fiscal Year 2023-24
  approved budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorical Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – the project
  consists of minor alterations to existing public right of way facilities. No
  potential for significant impacts to the environment are anticipated in this
  project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve plans and specifications for
  the Adaptive/Traffic Responsive Signal Control Project, award the contract to
  HHS Construction, LLC, and authorize the City Manager to execute
  Construction Contract No. 23-06 and approve a purchase order in the amount
  of $5,042,519.35 which includes a 10% construction contingency.

  H. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 82505, A 7-UNIT CONDOMINIUM
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 116 WEST MARSHALL STREET
  AND FINDING OF AN EXEMPTION FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  5
   The development project located at 116 West Marshall Street is a 7-unit
  condominium on a 12,251-square-foot-lot. The project includes demolishing
  the one-story 758 square-foot single-family residential unit. Staff and the
  City’s contract consultant for land surveying, RKA Consulting Group Inc. have
  reviewed the Final Parcel Map and determined that it is in compliance with
  the State Subdivision Map Act, Conditions of Approval, and the City’s
  ordinances regarding subdivision.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) and is exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332, Class 32 exemption
  (In-Fill-Development).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council find the project exempt from CEQA
  based on Section 15332, Class 32 (In-Fill Development), approve Final Parcel
  Map No. 82505, authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf
  of the City.

  I. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 73548, A MIXED-USE
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 860 EAST VALLEY BOULEVARD
  AND FINDING OF AN EXEMPTION FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  The mixed-use development project located at 860 East Valley Boulevard
  consists of 49 residential condominium units and 9,145-square-foot retail uses
  on a 38,480-square-foot site at the southwest corner of Valley Boulevard and
  Charlotte Avenue. The project would assemble two parcels and redevelop the
  approximately 0.86-acre site. City staff and the Los Angeles County
  Department of Public Works have reviewed the Final Tract Map and have
  determined it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, Conditions
  of Approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivision.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) and is exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332, Class 32 exemption
  (In-Fill-Development). The planning commission approved the project on May
  11, 2020. In compliance with Section 66412.3 of the Subdivision Map Act, the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  6
   Planning Commission has determined that the subdivision is consistent with the
  City’s actions with regards to the region’s housing needs.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council find the project exempt from CEQA on
  Section 15332, Class 32 (In-Fill Development), approve Final Tract Map No.
  73548, and authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

  J. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 83378, AND A SUBDIVISION
  IMPROVEMENT AGREEMENT FOR A 10-UNIT, MULTI-FAMILY
  RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 216-220 EAST
  BROADWAY AND FINDING OF A CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT EXEMPTION

  The development, located at 216-220 East Broadway, is a three-story multi-
  family residential development with 10 residential units on a 10,018 square
  foot (0.23 acre) site. Staff and RKA Consulting Group, Inc., the City’s contract
  consultant for land surveying, have reviewed the Final Tract Map and
  determined that it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, the
  City’s Conditions of Approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding
  subdivisions.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) and is exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332, Class 32 exemption
  (In-Fill-Development).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council find the project exempt from CEQA
  based on Section 15332, Class 32 (In-Fill Development), approve Final Tract
  Map No. 83378 and the Subdivision Improvement Agreement, authorize its
  filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the Subdivision Agreement.

  K. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JMDIAZ, INCORPORATED
  FOR ENGINEERING ENTITLEMENT PLAN REVIEW SERVICES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $124,800 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-24

  Award of a Professional Services Agreement with JMDiaz, Inc. for engineering
  entitlement plan review services for a term of three years. The City has an
  ongoing need for supplemental staff assistance for large-scale engineering

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  7
   entitlement reviews and processes. The services provided under the
  Agreement are paid for by fees paid and/or deposited by project applicants to
  cover the actual cost of the service. The costs are estimated at $124,800 for
  fiscal year 2023-24 based on an hourly billing rate of $100 and past level of
  service needs. The rates will be subject to a three percent annual increase.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a Professional Services
  Agreement with JMDiaz, Inc. to provide engineering entitlement plan review
  services for the terms mentioned above.

  L. STREET BANNER REQUEST – KIDS KLUB CHILD DEVELOPMENT CENTER

  The Public Works Department received a request to hang a street banner on
  San Gabriel Boulevard at Broadway for the Kids Klub Child Development
  Center from November 21, 2023, to December 21, 2023. Normally-scheduled
  staff time will be used for this item. As per the fee schedule, the $285.00
  banner fee is waived for non-profits.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council grant the request to hang the street
  banner at San Gabriel Boulevard and Broadway, subject to compliance with
  Section 153.334(A) of the Municipal Code and the street banner conditions as
  listed on Page 2 of the street banner application form.

  M. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-17 TO ROYAL ROOF TO
  REPLACE THE ROOF AT SOUTH FIRE STATION #51 LOCATED AT 1303
  SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE IN THE AMOUNT OF $73,700 PLUS A 20%
  CONTINGENCY

  This item requests Council’s award of a construction contract to Royal Roof, as
  the lowest responsive bidder to re-roof the main facility of the South Fire
  Station #51 for a cost of $73,700 plus a 20% Contingency of $14,740. Funds
  are available in the Fiscal Year 2023-24 approved budget.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  8
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as roof replacement
  does not have a potential to result in direct physical change in the environment,
  or a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council award the contract to Royal Roofing
  and authorize the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23-17
  and approve a purchase order in the amount of $88,440 which includes a 20%
  construction contingency.

  N. 2024 SAN GABRIEL LUNAR LANTERN FESTIVAL – PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MRBI/KAZN FOR EVENT PLANNING AND
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES

  Since 2016, the City of San Gabriel has hosted a Lunar New Year Festival in the
  Mission District. For the 2024 event, celebrating the Year of the Dragon, staff
  proposes that the City work with media partner MRBI/KAZN (KAZN) to host
  the Lunar Lantern Festival, a two-day event to be held on Saturday, February
  17, from 10:00 a.m. – 9:00 p.m. and Sunday, February 18, from 10:00 a.m. –
  7:00 p.m. As part of the Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget, the City Council allocated
  funding for community engagement events with a portion of that funding
  designated for the 9th Annual Lunar Lantern Festival. Event costs will be
  covered by KAZN media group and associated sponsors. In-kind costs of staff
  time for street closures, public safety personnel, etc. will be covered by the
  City. Additionally, the costs of the welcome gathering for dignitaries, which
  are approximately $300, will be covered by the City.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as a short two-day event
  will not have any foreseeable impacts on the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the proposal and draft the
  Professional Servies Agreement to authorize KAZN to host the 2024 Lunar
  Lantern Festival and authorize the City Manager to sign the final agreement
  and any other documents necessary to implement the agreement.

  O. ACCEPTANCE OF $5,000 COMMUNITY GRANT FROM THE CITY OF HOPE
  FOR THE SG MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION
  NO. 23-68

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  9
   The City of Hope donated $5,000 in support of the San Gabriel Mental
  Wellness Expo. The money was provided as part of the Community Grant in
  support of the live translation services in Spanish and Mandarin offered at the
  Expo. This report is to accept and acknowledge the donation and request the
  City Council to approve Resolution No. 23-68 amending Fiscal Year 2023-2024
  budget to reflect the donation. Adoption of the Resolution will result in an
  increase of $5,000 in the donations revenue account number 121-3920 and
  appropriating $5,000 from that account to Community Services Special Event
  expenditure account number 121-850-10-23-047.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept a donation of $5,000 from the
  City of Hope and adopt Resolution No. 23-68.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 693 AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE, VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC PLAN, AND MISSION
  DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN RELATING TO OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS
  FOR MULTI-FAMILY AND MIXED-USE PROJECTS (ZTA23-002) –
  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  In recent years, the State of California has been in an ongoing housing supply
  crisis. As a result, numerous laws have been passed by the State to help
  alleviate the housing shortage. At the March 2, 2023 joint City Council and
  Planning Commission study session, Staff presented an informational staff
  report summarizing the new bills and legislation as well as draft language for
  the Objective Design Standards. The City Council directed Planning staff to
  work with the City Architect and the Design Review Commission to finalize the
  Objective Design Standards and prepare an ordinance. A draft ordinance was
  provided to the Design Review Commission and the Planning Commission for
  further consideration and recommendation on May 22, 2023 and August 14,
  2023, respectively. Following further discussions, the Planning Commission
  recommended approval to the City Council of the proposed zone text
  amendment (ZTA23-002) for Ordinance No. 693. Impact fees will be charged
  for new development in accordance with City requirements, but because this
  project does not directly result in specific development, the financial impacts
  to the City, if any, are unknown at this time.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  10
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendment would be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  under Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA guidelines, under the common sense
  exemption, because it can be seen with certainty that it would not have
  significant effect on the environment and, thus, is not subject to CEQA review.

  Recommended Action:
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 693.
  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 693 by title only;
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE),
  THE VALLEY BOULEVARD NEIGHBORHOODS SUSTAINABILITY PLAN,
  AND THE MISSION DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN TO INCORPORATE
  OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS FOR MULTI-FAMILY AND MIXED-
  USE DEVELOPMENTS.
  3. Waive further reading and schedule the second reading and adoption of
  Ordinance No. 693 for the next regular City Council meeting. The
  ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Alternative Option for Consideration:

  Provide comments and direct staff to return at a later date with revisions to
  the amendment for the City Council’s review and approval.

  B. ORDINANCE NO. 695 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO MIXED-USE STANDARDS IN THE C-1
  AND C-3 ZONE DISTRICTS (ZTA23-003) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST
  READING

  The proposed Zone Text Amendment would amend Chapter 153 of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code relating to Mixed-Use Standards in the C-1 and C-3
  Zone Districts. The proposed Zone Text Amendment is intended to implement
  the goals and programs identified in the 2021-2029 Housing Element. The
  Fiscal Year 2022-23 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal
  publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No.
  121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with CEQA. An Initial

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  11
   Study/Negative Declaration was prepared to the 2021-2029 Housing Element,
  as required by the California Environmental Quality Act, Public Resources Code
  Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA guidelines, and the City of San Gabriel Local
  Guidelines for Implementing CEQA. The Initial Study/Negative Declaration
  considered the policies and programs outlined in the Housing Element. The
  Housing Element establishes objectives, policies, and programs to assist the City
  in achieving state-mandated housing goals. No formal land use changes or
  physical development are proposed at this time and future land use and
  physical development would require separate environmental evaluation.

  Recommended Action:
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 695;
  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 695 by title only:
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO MIXED-USE STANDARDS IN
  THE C-1 AND C-3 ZONES.
  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next Regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  C. AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  EXTENDING EXISTING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR PROJECT NO.
  PL-15-149, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT, AND VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO. 74993 FOR
  THE SYMPHONY AT SAN GABRIEL ASSISTED LIVING PROJECT AT 806-
  824 SOUTH GLADYS AVENUE VIA ADOPTION OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO
  THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  On September 8, 2023, the representatives of the development project for
  806-824 S. Gladys Avenue submitted a request to extend the Planned
  Development and Development Agreement and Vesting Tentative Parcel Map
  No. 74993 for the Elegance Senior Assisted Living Project (Planning Case No.
  PL-15-149) from January 4, 2023 to January 4, 2024. Pursuant to Section 5.02
  of the Development Agreement, City Council has the authority to approve an
  amendment extending the term of the Development Agreement. There is no
  negative fiscal impact as it relates to this request for extension. Should the
  extension not be approved, this project would most likely not move forward
  reducing the potential property tax revenue for the City.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  12
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The Mitigated
  Negative Declaration adopted in conjunction with the Project remains valid and
  in effect and continues to be the proper and legal environmental document for
  the Project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 698;
  2. Motion to waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 698 by title
  only;
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  EXTENDING EXISTING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR PROJECT NO.
  PL-15-149, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT, AND VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO. 74993 FOR
  THE SYMPHONY AT SAN GABRIEL ASSISTED LIVING PROJECT AT 806-
  824 SOUTH GLADYS AVENUE VIA ADOPTION OF FIRST AMENDMENT
  TO THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT
  3. Motion to waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second
  reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council
  meeting. The ordinance would then become effective 30 days after
  adoption.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. DISCUSSION AND POTENTIAL COUNCIL DIRECTION REGARDING THE
  STREET NAME CHANGE GUIDELINES

  On May 3, 2022, the City Council directed staff to draft guidelines for street
  name changes. To help facilitate the drafting of such guidelines, the City
  Council directed staff to solicitate feedback and comments from the HEAR
  Commission, Planning Commission, and the Historic Preservation and Cultural
  Resources Commission. At the February 7, 2023 City Council meeting, the City
  Council directed staff to seek direction from the Historic Preservation and
  Cultural Resources Commission regarding the definition of a legacy business
  and the number of years to be deemed eligible. At the September 13, 2023
  Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission meeting, the
  Commission provided feedback and comments regarding the definition for a
  legacy business. The application fee will be $768 plus the plan check fee for
  Public Works which is based on staff’s fully burden rate plus outside costs.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 7, 2023  13
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378(b)(5) of the State CEQA Guidelines as adoption of a
  policy is not organizational or administrative activity which will result in direct,
  or indirect physical change to the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the matter and provide
  direction to staff regarding the new policy or guidelines.

  In addition, the Council may also elect to amend the application procedures
  to require an application to go before the HEAR Commission and the Historic
  Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission before proceeding to the
  City Council for final consideration.

  7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The regular City Council meeting scheduled for November 21, 2023 has been
  cancelled. The Regular Meeting of the City Council on December 5, 2023 will start
  at 7:30 pm following the holiday tree-lighting event. Information regarding
  matters to be considered at each meeting will be available on the Friday before
  the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 7, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:31 P.M. on Tuesday, November 7, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Menchaca.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Fire Division
  Chief Newton Ong, Police Chief Edward Elizalde,
  Assistant Finance Director Linda Tang, and Assistant City
  Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

I  A. NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH

  Mayor Harrington made the presentation and Chief Anthony Morales, Gabrieleno
  San Gabriel Band of Mission Indians, and Nadine Salas and Chairman Andy Salas
  of the Kizh Nation San Gabrieleno Band of Mission Indians, accepted the
  proclamation.

  B. LUNG CANCER AWARENESS MONTH

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 9  November 7, 2023
   Mayor Harrington made the presentation.

  C. UNITED AGAINST HATE WEEK

  Mayor Harrington made the presentation and Asian Youth Center Community
  Relations Manager Florence Lin and Stop the Hate Manager Heidi Lau accepted
  the proclamation.

  D. ATHENS SERVICES UPDATE

I  Athens Services Director of Government Affairs Becky Cheng made the
  presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Dan Gosserand provided comments thanking all who contributed to the fund raiser for
  Police K9 Officer Barada.

  Andrew, resident, expressed his support of United Against Hate Week, commented on
  the passing of his uncle, Alfonso Lopez, and commended the Community Services
  Department's Dia de Los Muertos event.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Vice Mayor Wu pulled item 4L for separate consideration. Discussion included more
  details about the Kids Klub Development Center and this event, the organization's
  non-profit status, tuition details, precedent concerns for granting a waiver, and desire
  for clearer guidelines for the future.

I  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Ding, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 40 as presented, with a request to
  clarify policy guidelines for the future in relation to item 4L.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4- 1 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  WU
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of
  October 17, 2023.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

I  The City Council approved October 6, 2023, October 13, 2023, and October 20,
  2023, Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2023 FOR
  THE GENERAL FUND AND MISSION PLAYHOUSE FUND

  The City Council received and filed the report.

  D. CITY CYBER SECURITY APPLICATION SUBSCRIPTION IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $40,513

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 9  November 7, 2023
 •

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to enter into a subscription
  agreement with DarkTrace Cyber Security application in the amount of $40,513
  from July 17, 2023 to September 29, 2025.

  E. 2024 CITY COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE

  The City Council approved the 2024 City Council meeting schedule as outlined in
  the staff report.

  I  F. RESOLUTION NO. 23-70 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED SALARY SCHEDULE
  TO INCORPORATE THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA 2024 MINIMUM WAGE RATE

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-70, which amends the City's
  authorized Salary Schedule by increasing the pay range of all part-time position
  classifications by the 2024 minimum wage requirement, effective December 30,
  2023, and increases the General Fund appropriations $7,890 and various other
  special funds $6,447 to cover increases costs to part-time position salaries for FY
  2023-24.

  G. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-06 TO HHS CONSTRUCTION LLC
  FOR THE ADAPTIVE/TRAFFIC RESPONSIVE SIGNAL CONTROL PROJECT IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $4,584,108.50 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  The City Council approved plans and specifications for the Adaptive/Traffic
  Responsive Signal Control Project, awarded the contract to HHS Construction, LLC,
  and authorized the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23-06 and
  approve a purchase order in the amount of $5,042,519.35 which includes a 10%

  I  construction contingency.

  H. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 82505, A 7-UNIT CONDOMINIUM
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 116 WEST MARSHALL STREET AND
  FINDING OF AN EXEMPTION FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT

  The City Council found the project exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332,
  Class 32 (In-Fill Development), approved Final Parcel Map No. 82505, authorized
  its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorized the City Manager
  to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

  I. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 73548, A MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT
  PROJECT LOCATED AT 860 EAST VALLEY BOULEVARD AND FINDING OF AN
  EXEMPTION FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  The City Council found the project exempt from CEQA on Section 15332, Class 32
  (In-Fill Development), approved Final Tract Map No. 73548, and authorized its filing

  I  with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

  J. APPROVAL OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 83378, AND A SUBDIVISION
  IMPROVEMENT AGREEMENT FOR A 10-UNIT, MULTI-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 216-220 EAST BROADWAY AND
  FINDING OF A CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT EXEMPTION

  The City Council found the project exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332,
  Class 32 (In-Fill Development), approved Final Tract Map No. 83378 and the
  Subdivision Improvement Agreement, authorized its filing with the Los Angeles

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 9  November 7, 2023
   County Recorder and authorized the City Manager to execute the Subdivision
  Agreement.
  K. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JMDIAZ, INCORPORATED FOR
  ENGINEERING ENTITLEMENT PLAN REVIEW SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $124,800 FOR FISCAL VEAR 2023-24

  The City Council approved a Professional Services Agreement with JMDiaz, Inc. to
  provide engineering entitlement plan review services for a three-year term.

I  L. STREET BANNER REQUEST - KIDS KLUB CHILD DEVELOPMENT CENTER

  The City Council granted the request to hang the street banner at San Gabriel
  Boulevard and Broadway, subject to compliance with Section 153.334(A) of the
  Municipal Code and the street banner conditions as listed on Page 2 of the street
  banner application form.

  M. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-17 TO ROYAL ROOF TO
  REPLACE THE ROOF AT SOUTH FIRE STATION #51 LOCATED AT 1303 SOUTH
  DEL MAR AVENUE IN THE AMOUNT OF $73,700 PLUS A 20% CONTINGENCY

  The City Council awarded the contract to Royal Roofing and authorized the City
  Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23-17 and approve a purchase
  order in the amount of $88,440 which includes a 20% construction contingency.

  N. 2024 SAN GABRIEL LUNAR LANTERN FESTIVAL - PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH MRBI/KAZN FOR EVENT PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT
  SERVICES

I  The City Council approved the proposal and Professional Services Agreement to
  authorize KAZN to host the 2024 Lunar Lantern Festival and authorized the City
  Manager to sign the final agreement and any other documents necessary to
  implement the agreement.

  0. ACCEPTANCE OF $5,000 COMMUNITY GRANT FROM THE CITY OF HOPE FOR
  THE SG MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 23-
  68

  The City Council accepted a donation of $5,000 from the City of Hope and adopted
  Resolution No. 23-68 amending Fiscal Year 2023-2024 budget to reflect the
  donation.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 693 AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE, VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC PLAN, AND MISSION
  DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN RELATING TO OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS FOR

I  MULTI-FAMILY AND MIXED-USE PROJECTS (ZTA23-002) - INTRODUCTION
  AND FIRST READING

  Mayor Harrington opened the public hearing.

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart, Senior Planner Christine Song, and
  Associate Planner Marlon Cervantes made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included how adoption of this ordinance would streamline
  and affect the development process; projects would be reviewed per current

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 9  November 7, 2023
   standards until implementation of this ordinance; recent legislation effects on
  timing for this ordinance coming to the City Council; and that the City has no
  current applications that will be affected.

  Senya Lubisich, resident, expressed concern in rushing these provisions and for
  protection for historical districts like the Mission District, and her desire to engage
  the Historic Preservation and Culture Resource Commission (HPCRC) in the
  process.

I  Mayor Harrington closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included kudos to the Design Review Commission (DRC) and Planning
  Commission (PC) for the questions they raised which resulted in staff making
  changes; how this ordinance will affect incentive to develop, the purpose of the
  ordinance is to streamline the review process; effect on undeveloped properties;
  importance, process, and timeline for historical preservation; the ordinance would
  affect commercial but not residential properties; preservation requires
  collaboration with the property owner; how other cities are dealing with these
  standards; fast-tracking historic preservation of properties in commercia l corridors;
  the process for local historical designation has not been formally defined; the
  zoning affected by Senate Bills 6 and 35; and the ability to amend the ordinance in
  the future.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 693 by title only;
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,

I  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE), THE VALLEY
  BOULEVARD NEIGHBORHOODS SUSTAINABILITY PLAN, AND THE MISSION
  DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN TO INCORPORATE OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS
  FOR MULTI-FAMILY AND MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENTS.
  2. Waive further reading and schedule the second reading and adoption of
  Ordinance No. 693 for the next regular City Council meeting.

  3. Fast-track designation of local historic properties and monitor other cities
  actions on this matter.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. ORDINANCE NO. 695 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO MIXED-USE STANDARDS IN THE C-1 AND C-

I  3 ZONE DISTRICTS (ZTA23-003) - INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the staff presentation.

  Mayor Harrington opened the public hearing. There was no public comment;
  therefore, Mayor Harrington closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included disagreement with raising the height limit for mixed-use
  development to five stories; existing five story developments in the City were
  approved through a planned-development overlay zone or specific plan; if the
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 9  November 7, 2023
   ordinance is not approved for five stories, staff will have to go back to figure out
  how to comply with meeting the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA)
  numbers mandated by the State; mixed-use requires parcels of an acre or greater;
  the Valley Boulevard Specific Plan allows five-story mixed-use projects; listen;
  adoption of this ordinance would be giving up negotiation for a by-right process;
  details of RHNA requirements; residential zoning is limited as to height; fire life-
  safety issues with buildings over three stories due to equipment limitations;

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member

I  Chan, to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 695 by title only: AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF SAN GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA,
  AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO MIXED-USE STANDARDS IN THE C-1 AND C-3 ZONES, as
  amended to limit height to three stories in Ordinance Section 2((5) instead of
  the proposed five stories.
  2. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next Regular City Council meeting. The
  Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  C. AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  EXTENDING EXISTING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR PROJECT NO. PL-15-
  149, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT, AND
  VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO. 74993 FOR THE SYMPHONY AT SAN
  GABRIEL ASSISTED LIVING PROJECT AT 806-824 SOUTH GLADYS AVENUE
  VIA ADOPTION OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT
  - INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  Mayor Harrington opened the public hearing.

  Community Development Director Cervantes made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included that the name of the project has changed from
  Symphony to Elegance; this is the second request for an extension; the extension
  would be until January 2025; status of the project; and once approved, the project
  is vested under the then-current Building Code.

  Andrew, resident, expressed concerns with several aspects of the project.

I  Mayor Harrington closed the public hearing.

  Paul Griffin, representative for Elegance San Gabriel, presented information about
  the project.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 698 by title only;

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 6 of 9  November 7, 2023
   AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  EXTENDING EXISTING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR PROJECT NO. PL-15 -
  149, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT, AND
  VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO. 74993 FOR THE ELEGANCE AT SAN
  GABRIEL ASSISTED LIVING PROJECT AT 806-824 SOUTH GLADYS AVENUE VIA
  ADOPTION OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT.

  2. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.

I  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed at 9:41 P.M. and reconvened at 9:47 P.M. with all Council
  Members present.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. DISCUSSION AND POTENTIAL COUNCIL DIRECTION REGARDING THE STREET
  NAME CHANGE GUIDELINES

  Community Development Director Cervantes made the presentation.

I  Clarifying discussion included guidelines versus a policy; the City Council's previous
  direction was for staff to return with guidelines; proposed fee; clarifications
  requested in the proposed guidelines; department approvals before the
  application would go to Commissions; and there is currently only one request for
  street name change.

  Caren Lin, representing Hing Wa Lee Jewelers which has a request in with the City
  for a street-name change, spoke about benefits to the City of their business and in
  support of setting the threshold for legacy businesses with a range of years in the
  City.

  Andrew, resident, advocated for a minimum of 50 years in the City for a business
  to qualify as a legacy business.

  Discussion included that the Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource
  Commission (HPCRC) was emphatic for 50 years within the City of San Gabriel to
  qualify as a legacy business, agreement that the Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission and HPCRC should review applications; notification

I  of requests to change street names; order of review of applications by various
  entities; identification of stakeholders for notification for individual applications;
  getting recommendations from HEAR and HPCR Commissions for an award
  structure for legacy businesses; one request for a street-name change was received
  in the last 10 years; preference for a 30-year minimum and streamlining the process
  by having only one commission review requests; reservations about not allowing
  franchised or national chains to qualify as a legacy business; businesses
  headquartered or founded in San Gabriel should be eligible to be a legacy
  business, having the applicant cover expenses for noticing; a requirement for a
  certain percentage of home owners or businesses to consent; for the current
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 7 of 9  November 7, 2023
   request, the existing street for which a name change is requested has no
  residences; the possibility of handling requests on a case-by-case basis rather than
  having a policy; how other cities have handled street-name changes; and a
  preference for 20 years in the City to be a legacy business.

  A motion was made by Mayor Harrington, seconded by Council Member Chan, to
  accept all staff recommendations with a revision to designate 20 years in the City
  for a legacy business and for prior noticing to affected parties rather than post-
  noticing.

I  Motion carried by a vote of 4- 7 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  MENCHACA
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  7. NEW BUSINESS - None.
  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT - None.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Menchaca requested, with the agreement of Mayor Harrington and
  Council Member Chan, that an award structure for legacy businesses be agendized,
  and that staff put information on street vending on the City's website and social media.
  She commended Community Services Director Perez and Community Services

I  Manager Matthew Morales-Stephens for the flags displayed as a tribute to Veterans;
  thanked La Casa teachers, El Pavo Bakery, and staff for the well-attended Dia de Los
  Muertos event; gave a reminder about the Veterans lunch on November 9, 2023, at 12
  P.M. at the Mission Playhouse; and announced the first Veterans Day ceremony in the
  City on November 10, 2023.
  Vice Mayor Wu announced that City Hall is closed on November 10, 2023, and invited
  all to the Veterans Day ceremony on that date, at 10:00 A.M. across from City Hall.

  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at Ogopogo's 5th Anniversary
  celebration, the barbecue fund raiser for San Gabriel K9 Officer Barada, the San Gabriel
  Fall Fun Festival, San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce monthly networking event; and
  San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce Harvest dinner.

  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at a Sanitation District meeting and
  San Gabriel Council of Governments (COG) Energy and Transportation meeting and
  reported that the San Gabriel Hope Lions Club assisted the City in the distribution of
  cookie boxes to seniors.

  Mayor Harrington thanked staff for the Veterans Day display.

I  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Harrington announced that the regular City Council meeting scheduled for
  November 21, 2023, had been cancelled and that the regular City Council meeting
  scheduled for December 5, 2023, would have a delayed start at 7:30 pm following the
  holiday tree-lighting event.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 8 of 9  November 7, 2023
   The meeting was adjourned at 11 :07 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

I  Approved this 5th day of December, 2023:
